title: embeddings-rerank-latency-dim-mismatch-scratch-maya-2026-03-15
content:
Quick dump of debugging notes for the embeddings->rerank incident (dim mismatch + latency spikes)

Summary:
- Customer-facing rerank pipeline started failing intermittently on 2026-03-11 with errors around vector dimension mismatch.
- Around same time we saw p95 token latency for the rerank endpoint spike from ~120ms to ~900ms for some requests.
- Repro locally on staging with smaller traffic; root cause unclear (model variant change? inference runtime fallback?).

Timeline / observable facts:
- 2026-03-11 02:14 UTC: First SLO alert for rerank-prod p95 > 500ms.
- 2026-03-11 02:15-02:40: multiple errors in rerank service logs: DimensionMismatchError for 12% of requests.
- 2026-03-11 02:41: engineering rollback of a recent quantization profile on dedicated-pool-3 (suspected).
- 2026-03-11 03:00: p95 improved but not back to baseline; some clients still hit dimension mismatch.
- 2026-03-12 - ongoing: intermittent reappearance on prod and staging.

Observed metrics (prod approx):
- normal baseline: rerank p50 ~ 80ms, p95 ~ 120ms
- incident windows: rerank p50 ~ 130ms, p95 ~ 900ms (tail driven by retries + fallback)
- error rate for rerank (5xx) peaked at 3.7%
- % requests with DimensionMismatchError ~ 0.8% overall, spikes to ~12% on some host windows

Representative error log snippets:
1) Dimension mismatch (from rerank-service logs):
[2026-03-11T02:17:12.493Z] ERROR rerank: failed to compute dot-product: DimensionMismatchError: expected vector length=1024 but got 1536 for embedding id=usr-8a2b
stack: at rerank.computeScores (score.js:142)
 at rerank.handleRequest (server.js:88)

2) Client-facing error returned (example):
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "DimensionMismatchError: expected 1024, got 1536",
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d"
}

3) Latency-related traces (from trace-id trace-9f1e):
- embedding generation (model=open-embed-large-1536): 480ms
- KV cache lookup: 8ms
- rerank scoring (dot-product CPU fallback): 320ms
- overhead/retries: 110ms
(note: we see fallback to CPU for scoring in cases where GPU execution failed)

Commands / queries I ran (local/staging):
- curl to embeddings endpoint to check dims:
  curl -X POST "https://staging.redwood/api/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"openembed-small-1024","input":"hello"}' | jq .data[0].embedding | length
  -> 1024 (expected)

- Tested model variant that returns 1536 dims:
  curl -X POST "https://staging.redwood/api/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"openembed-large-1536","input":"hello"}' | jq .data[0].embedding | length
  -> 1536 (expected)

- Ran a sampling script to detect mixed-dim batches (python snippet):
  - iterate over last 1000 requests in S3 logs, parse embedding.dim, count distinct dims per request-id.
  Result: ~2.7% of requests contained mixed dims in the same multi-request payload (some clients sending batched queries with different model ids).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Client/batch issue: callers are accidentally batching inputs that use different embedding models (1024 vs 1536). Our rerank pipeline expects a fixed dim and doesn't detect model id per item (fast-path assumption). Evidence: logs show mixed dims inside same request in ~2.7% sample.
2) Model routing mismatch: smart-routing layer returned a different model variant for the same customer during rolling deploy/scale (e.g., fallback to openembed-large-1536 on some workers). Evidence: trace shows embedding model name mismatch in a subset of traces.
3) Runtime quantization/profile change: one of the dedicated nodes applied a quantization profile that altered the dimensionality (less likely since models shouldn't change vector size).
4) Inference fallback from GPU->CPU led to different code path that trims/pads embeddings incorrectly (possible bug).

Immediate mitigations attempted (and results):
- Hotfix: added server-side validation to reject batched requests with mixed embedding dims (deploy to staging then prod hotfix): reduced DimensionMismatchError to near-zero for new requests but didn't resolve already-queued requests.
- Rollback: we rolled back quantization change on dedicated-pool-3 (March 11 02:41) — latency improved but mixed-dim errors persisted.
- Rate-limit and fail-fast: added a temporary gate to fail requests if embedding dim != expected for route. This prevented incorrect results from reaching user but caused small increase in 429s.

Open questions / things to confirm:
- Are clients intentionally mixing different models in one batch? Check top 10 customer SDK versions and their batching logic. (Jordan to reach out to CS).
- Does the routing layer ever rewrite model id or substitute a model that produces different dims? Look at router logs between 02:00-03:00 UTC 2026-03-11. (Liam to check).
- Do any of the embedder families produce variable-length embeddings due to experimental compression? (Research/Applied-ML)

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add server-side check earlier in pipeline to tag requests with embedding.model_id per input and enforce single-model batches (done as hotfix, need to harden in mainline).
- [ ] Add a telemetry metric: embedding_dim_distribution per route (histogram) and alert when multiple dims seen in same customer request.
- [ ] Instrument router to record model_id returned for each request and persist in traces (correlate with request_id).
- [ ] Run retrospective on deploy/rollback timeline to see if routing changes coincide with spikes. (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Reach out to top affected customers (CS) with remediation and ask for any SDK batching code snippets. (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Add unit/integration test: rerank pipeline should raise clear error if dims mismatch and avoid expensive CPU fallback scoring; add regression for CPU fallback path.

Notes from quick experiments:
- When server-side validation rejects mixed-dim batches early, overall p95 drops back to ~140ms but p99 still elevated in a few windows (likely due to retries and downstream queueing).
- CPU fallback scoring path adds ~300ms when invoked; need to handle fallback more gracefully (e.g., queue and recompute or reject earlier).

Follow-ups for applied-ml team:
- Confirm that none of the new model variants we onboarded last 6 weeks change embedding dimensionality unexpectedly. If any do, update model catalog metadata with embedding_dim field and ensure routing respects model families.

Scratch list of quick commands to run next: 
- grep -R "DimensionMismatchError" /var/log/rerank/* | sed -n '1,200p'
- python tools/scan_logs.py --start 2026-03-11T00:00 --end 2026-03-12T00:00 --field embedding_dim --aggregate-by request_id | jq .
- curl "https://prod.redwood/api/v1/debug/router/last_routes?since=2026-03-11T02:00&until=2026-03-11T03:00&route=rerank" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

Quick conclusions for postmortem draft:
- Immediate cause: mixed-dimension embedding vectors in batched requests + rerank pipeline assumed homogenous dims -> thrown DimensionMismatchError and fallback to expensive CPU scoring path for some requests causing latency spikes.
- Contributing factors: lack of model_id tagging per input in early pipeline, routing layer variance during deployment window, insufficient telemetry for embedding_dim per route.
- Remediation: server-side validation, telemetry + alerts, router instrumentation, client SDK guidance (avoid mixing models in one batch).

Notes end.

-- Maya
